name: webpack-resolve-fallback-node-false-for-node-protocol
hook: resolve.fallback node:false is the correct webpack 5 API for node: protocol imports
body: webpack 5's resolve.fallback with { node: false } is the correct mechanism for handling Node.js built-in module requests via the node: protocol (node:console, node:crypto, node:dns, etc.). It returns an empty object, satisfying the resolver without actually polyfilling. Do NOT use resolve.alias with a regex pattern like '^node:(.*)$' — this is treated as a literal key in webpack 5 and never matches.
why: CI failed with 'UnhandledSchemeError: Reading from node:console is not handled by plugins'. The previous approach used resolve.alias with '^node:(.*)$' which does not work because webpack 5 resolve.alias treats string keys literally, not as regex.

name: next-config-js-uses-esm-require-unavailable
hook: next.config.js is ESM — use path.resolve not require.resolve
body: next.config.js uses ESM (import at top level), so require is not available. When adding webpack resolve.alias entries that need a file path, use path.resolve(process.cwd(), ...) instead of require.resolve(...). process.cwd() gives the project root at build time.
why: CI failed with 'ReferenceError: require is not defined' at next.config.js because the file is ESM but required was used in the webpack config callback.

name: externalize-metapackage-also-externalize-platform-packages
hook: Externalizing a metapackage requires regex pattern to catch resolved platform-specific packages
body: When a metapackage like @napi-rs/canvas resolves to platform-specific packages (@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-gnu, @napi-rs/canvas-darwin-x64, etc.), simply adding the metapackage name to webpack externals is insufficient. Webpack resolves the platform-specific name and those packages are not in externals. Use a regex external pattern like /^@napi-rs\/canvas-/ to catch all platform variants.
why: CI failed with 'Node.js binary module ...skia.linux-x64-gnu.node is not supported in the browser' because @napi-rs/canvas was externalized but @napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-gnu was not, even though the former is just a metapackage that resolves to the latter.

name: node-binary-files-need-resolve-alias
hook: resolve.alias with .node$ regex key redirects .node native binary files to empty stub
body: The next-error-browser-binary-loader throws 'not supported in browser' for all .node files. To prevent this, use resolve.alias with a regex key matching .node files: webpackConfig.resolve.alias = { ...existing, '\\.node$': path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'src/server/utils/empty-stub.js') }. Webpack 5's resolve.alias DOES support regex keys. The regex '\.node$' matches any file path ending in .node and redirects it to the empty stub before the error-checker runs.
why: CI also failed with 'Node.js binary module ...skia.linux-x64-gnu.node is not supported in the browser'. The regex externals for @napi-rs/canvas-* were not sufficient because next-error-browser-binary-loader runs on .node files before the external check.
